# Imaging Apparatus with Distributed Image Recognition Support

## Technical Field

The present disclosure concerns an imaging apparatus, an image sensor, and an image processor. More specifically, the disclosed technology relates to systems designed to reduce the computational load imposed on an image processing unit during image recognition processing.

## Background and Overview

In conventional imaging systems, the burden of image recognition processing typically falls entirely upon a dedicated image processing unit. This concentration of computational demand can create performance bottlenecks and increase power consumption. The present disclosure addresses these challenges by distributing certain preparatory tasks to the image sensor itself, thereby easing the processing requirements of the downstream image processing unit.

## The Image Sensor

At the core of the disclosed technology is an image sensor comprising an array of photoelectric conversion elements arranged both vertically and horizontally across an imaging surface. These elements convert incident light into electrical signals through photoelectric conversion, generating pixel signals that collectively form the image data output by the sensor.

## Area-Based Support Information Generation

A distinguishing feature of this technology is the division of the imaging surface into multiple discrete areas. Rather than treating the imaging surface as a single undifferentiated field, the sensor processes each area independently. For every such area, the sensor generates image recognition support information derived from the pixel signals produced by the photoelectric conversion elements located within that particular area.

This localized approach allows relevant recognition-related data to be prepared at the sensor level, closer to the source of the raw image data, before it is transmitted onward for further processing.

## Cooperative Processing by the Image Processing Unit

The image processing unit receives both the output image data and the image recognition support information provided by the image sensor. Leveraging this support information, the image processing unit applies predetermined image processing to the output image data. Because a portion of the recognition-related workload has already been handled by the sensor, the image processing unit can perform its tasks more efficiently, with a correspondingly reduced computational load.

## Applications

The disclosed technology is well suited to a range of devices that rely on image recognition capabilities. In particular, it may be applied to cameras equipped with a face detection function, where efficient and responsive recognition processing is especially valuable. By offloading preparatory recognition tasks to the image sensor, such devices can achieve improved performance while maintaining lower processing overhead.

# Reducing Processing Load in Image Recognition Systems

## Technical Field

This disclosure relates to an image sensor and image processing system designed to reduce the computational burden associated with image recognition tasks. More specifically, it addresses methods for distributing recognition-related processing between an image sensor and a downstream image processing unit to achieve more efficient operation.

## Background

Conventional image recognition systems typically capture a full image using an image sensor and then transfer the entire image data to a separate processing unit, which performs all recognition-related computations. As image resolutions have increased and recognition tasks have grown more sophisticated, this approach places a substantial processing load on the image processing unit. Tasks such as face detection, object recognition, and feature extraction require analyzing large volumes of pixel data, which can result in slower response times, higher power consumption, and increased hardware requirements.

## Summary of the Disclosure

To address these challenges, this disclosure introduces an image sensor that performs preliminary analysis directly at the sensor level, thereby offloading a portion of the processing that would otherwise be handled entirely by the image processing unit.

The imaging surface of the image sensor is divided into multiple distinct areas, each containing a group of photoelectric conversion elements that convert incoming light into pixel signals. Rather than simply outputting raw pixel data for the entire frame, the image sensor generates **image recognition support information** for each individual area based on the pixel signals produced by the photoelectric conversion elements within that specific area.

This support information may include, for example, indications of regions likely to contain features of interest, preliminary classifications, edge or contrast characteristics, or other locally derived metadata that can assist subsequent recognition steps. By computing this information on a per-area basis, the sensor provides a structured, pre-analyzed representation of the scene alongside or in place of the full raw image.

## Operation of the Image Processing Unit

The image processing unit receives the image recognition support information generated by the image sensor and applies predetermined image processing based on this information. Because certain preliminary analysis has already been performed at the sensor level, the image processing unit does not need to examine every pixel of the entire frame with equal effort. Instead, it can direct its processing resources toward the areas identified as relevant by the support information.

For instance, in a camera performing face detection, the support information may indicate which areas of the imaging surface are likely to contain facial features. The image processing unit can then concentrate its detection algorithms on those specific areas, rather than scanning the whole image uniformly. This targeted approach significantly reduces the amount of data that must be fully processed and lowers the overall computational load.

## Advantages

By dividing the imaging surface into multiple areas and generating recognition support information locally for each area, the disclosed system achieves several benefits:

- **Reduced processing load**: The image processing unit performs less exhaustive computation, since the sensor has already provided guidance on where relevant features are located.
- **Improved efficiency**: Recognition tasks such as face detection can be completed more quickly and with fewer resources.
- **Lower power consumption**: Distributing the workload and reducing redundant processing can decrease overall energy usage.
- **Scalability**: The area-based approach adapts well to higher-resolution sensors, since analysis is partitioned across the imaging surface.

## Conclusion

In summary, this disclosure provides an image sensor and image processing arrangement in which the imaging surface is divided into multiple areas, and image recognition support information is generated for each area based on the corresponding pixel signals. The image processing unit then applies predetermined processing using this support information, enabling more efficient execution of recognition tasks such as face detection in cameras while reducing the overall processing burden.

# The Word "The"

The word **"the"** is one of the most fundamental and frequently used words in the English language. Known as the **definite article**, it plays an essential role in everyday communication, helping speakers and writers point to specific people, places, things, or ideas.

## What Makes "The" Special

Despite being only three letters long, "the" is the most commonly used word in English. It appears in nearly every sentence, conversation, and piece of writing. Its primary job is to signal that a noun refers to something specific or already known, as opposed to something general.

For example:
- "I saw **a** dog" (any dog, unspecified)
- "I saw **the** dog" (a particular dog we already know about)

## Grammatical Function

As a definite article, "the" is used with both singular and plural nouns, as well as with countable and uncountable nouns. This flexibility sets it apart from the indefinite articles "a" and "an," which are only used with singular countable nouns.

We use "the" when:
- The listener knows which thing we mean
- Something has been mentioned before
- There is only one of something (the sun, the moon)
- We refer to specific groups (the rich, the elderly)

## Origins and Pronunciation

The word "the" traces its roots back to Old English. Interestingly, its pronunciation can vary: it is typically pronounced "thuh" before consonant sounds and "thee" before vowel sounds.

## Conclusion

Though small and often overlooked, "the" is a cornerstone of English grammar. Its constant presence in our language highlights how even the simplest words can carry great importance in helping us communicate clearly and precisely.

---

# PATENT ABSTRACT

## Imaging Apparatus with Area-Based Image Recognition Support Information Generation

**Abstract:**

An imaging apparatus is disclosed that reduces the processing load on an image processing unit by generating image recognition support information on a per-area basis at the image sensor level. The apparatus comprises an image sensor configured to capture image data of a scene and divide the captured image into a plurality of areas. For each area, the image sensor generates recognition support information, which may include feature data, statistical parameters, edge information, or preliminary classification indicators characterizing the content of the respective area.

The image sensor transmits the generated recognition support information to a downstream image processing unit together with, or in association with, the captured image data. The image processing unit utilizes the pre-computed recognition support information to perform image recognition processing, thereby eliminating the need to independently analyze each area from raw image data. By offloading initial feature extraction and area characterization to the image sensor, the computational burden on the image processing unit is significantly reduced, enabling faster recognition processing and lower overall power consumption.

In certain embodiments, the recognition support information indicates which areas contain regions of interest, allowing the image processing unit to selectively allocate processing resources to relevant areas while disregarding or minimally processing other areas. The apparatus is suitable for applications including autonomous vehicles, surveillance systems, mobile devices, and other real-time image recognition environments where processing efficiency is critical.

---

*This abstract is provided as a template. Specific claims, technical details, and legal language should be reviewed and refined by a qualified patent attorney to ensure proper scope and compliance with applicable patent office requirements.*

# Summary of Invention

The present invention provides an image sensor and image processing system that divides an imaging surface into a plurality of areas to facilitate and enhance image recognition operations. It is an object of the present invention to overcome limitations of conventional imaging systems in which the entire imaging surface is processed uniformly, resulting in inefficient use of computational resources and reduced recognition accuracy.

## Overview

In accordance with one aspect of the present invention, an image sensor is provided that includes an imaging surface comprising a plurality of light-receiving elements arranged in a two-dimensional array. The imaging surface is logically divided into a plurality of areas, each area corresponding to a respective subset of the light-receiving elements. Each area may be configured to be read out, processed, or controlled independently of one or more other areas.

In accordance with another aspect, an image processor is coupled to the image sensor and is configured to receive image data from the plurality of areas. The image processor performs image recognition processing on the image data on a per-area basis, thereby enabling recognition operations to be tailored to the characteristics of individual areas.

## Advantageous Features

In certain embodiments, the division of the imaging surface into areas is dynamically adjustable. The size, shape, number, and location of the areas may be varied in response to one or more parameters, including but not limited to results of prior recognition processing, detected objects, scene conditions, or externally supplied control signals. This allows the system to allocate greater processing resources to areas of interest while reducing processing of areas deemed less relevant.

In further embodiments, the image sensor and image processor are configured to apply different imaging parameters to different areas. Such parameters may include exposure time, gain, frame rate, resolution, and readout timing. By independently controlling these parameters on a per-area basis, the system can optimize each area for its respective recognition task, such as applying a higher frame rate to areas containing moving objects and a higher resolution to areas requiring detailed feature extraction.

In still further embodiments, the image processor executes recognition processing on the areas in parallel, in sequence, or in a prioritized order. Recognition results obtained from one area may be used to influence the processing of another area, or to redefine the boundaries of the areas for subsequent frames.

In some embodiments, at least a portion of the image recognition processing is performed on-chip, within or in close proximity to the image sensor, thereby reducing the volume of data transferred to downstream processing components and lowering latency and power consumption.

## Benefits

By dividing the imaging surface into areas and processing those areas in the manner described herein, the present invention achieves one or more of the following benefits: improved recognition accuracy, reduced computational load, lower power consumption, decreased data transmission bandwidth, and reduced processing latency. These and other advantages of the present invention will become apparent from the following detailed description when taken in conjunction with the accompanying drawings.

---

*The foregoing summary is provided to introduce a selection of concepts in a simplified form and is not intended to identify essential features of the claimed subject matter, nor to limit the scope of the claimed subject matter.*

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to an imaging apparatus, and more particularly to an imaging apparatus including an image sensor configured to output support information usable to reduce the processing load of subject detection, such as face detection.

## Background

Conventional imaging apparatuses perform face detection in a processing circuit (e.g., an application processor or DSP) that analyzes full-resolution image data. This approach can impose a substantial computational load, increasing power consumption and latency, particularly in continuous or high-frame-rate operation.

## Summary — First Aspect of the Disclosure

**According to a first aspect of the present disclosure, there is provided an imaging apparatus comprising:**

- an **image sensor** including a pixel array configured to generate image data; and
- a **processing section** configured to perform detection processing on the image data,

wherein the image sensor is configured to generate **support information** based on the image data and to output the support information together with, or in association with, the image data, and

The **support information** may include, without limitation:

- a **region-of-interest (ROI) indication** identifying one or more candidate regions likely to contain a face or subject;
- **reduced-resolution or downscaled data** derived from the image data;
- **feature or edge information** (e.g., preliminary feature maps);

# Imaging Apparatus with Recognition Support Processing

## TECHNICAL FIELD

The present disclosure relates to an imaging apparatus, and more particularly to an imaging apparatus comprising an image sensor having photoelectric conversion elements and an image processing unit configured to perform image processing based on recognition support information.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

An imaging apparatus according to one embodiment of the present invention comprises the following elements as recited below.

## CLAIMS

**Claim 1.** An imaging apparatus comprising:

an image sensor including a plurality of photoelectric conversion elements arranged in a two-dimensional array, each of the photoelectric conversion elements being configured to generate an electric charge corresponding to an intensity of incident light and to output an image signal based on the generated electric charge; and

an image processing unit configured to acquire the image signal output from the image sensor and to generate image data by performing image processing on the acquired image signal,

wherein the image processing unit is further configured to obtain recognition support information relating to a subject represented in the image data, and to perform at least a portion of the image processing based on the obtained recognition support information.

**Claim 2.** The imaging apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the recognition support information includes at least one of: region information identifying a region of interest within the image data, category information indicating a class of the subject, and reliability information indicating a confidence level associated with a recognition result.

**Claim 3.** The imaging apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the image processing unit is configured to apply a first image processing parameter to a first region of the image data corresponding to the subject identified by the recognition support information, and to apply a second image processing parameter, different from the first image processing parameter, to a second region of the image data.

**Claim 4.** The imaging apparatus according to claim 1, further comprising a recognition unit configured to perform recognition processing on the image data using a trained model, and to generate the recognition support information based on a result of the recognition processing.

**Claim 5.** The imaging apparatus according to claim 4, wherein the image sensor and the recognition unit are disposed on a stacked semiconductor substrate, the image sensor being disposed on a first substrate and the recognition unit being disposed on a second substrate laminated to the first substrate.

**Claim 6.** The imaging apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the image processing unit is configured to determine at least one of a noise reduction strength, a sharpening strength, a tone correction characteristic, and a color correction characteristic based on the recognition support information.

**Claim 7.** The imaging apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the recognition support information is generated from a first frame of the image data, and the image processing unit applies the recognition support information to image processing of a second frame subsequent to the first frame.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION

### Overview of the Apparatus

In the following description, reference is made to embodiments of the imaging apparatus. It should be understood that the described embodiments are illustrative and are not intended to limit the scope of the claims.

Referring to the configuration of the imaging apparatus, the **image sensor** comprises a plurality of **photoelectric conversion elements** (for example, photodiodes) arranged in rows and columns. Each photoelectric conversion element converts incident light received through an optical system into an electric charge, wherein an amount of the electric charge corresponds substantially to an intensity of the incident light integrated over an exposure period. A readout circuit reads out the accumulated electric charge and converts the electric charge into an image signal, which may be an analog signal subsequently converted to a digital signal by an analog-to-digital converter.

### Image Processing Unit

The **image processing unit** receives the image signal and performs one or more image processing operations, which may include, without limitation, demosaicing, white balance adjustment, noise reduction, gamma correction, color conversion, and compression encoding. In accordance with the present embodiment, the image processing unit obtains **recognition support information** and modifies at least one of the aforementioned image processing operations in dependence upon the recognition support information.

### Recognition Support Information

As used herein, the term "recognition support information" refers to information that assists the image processing unit in adapting the image processing to characteristics of a subject appearing within the captured scene. By way of example, and not by way of limitation, the recognition support information may comprise coordinate data defining a bounding region enclosing a detected subject, a label indicating a semantic category of the subject (such as a person, a face, a vehicle, or vegetation), and a probability value representing an estimated reliability of the detection.

In one embodiment, the image processing unit selectively varies image processing parameters spatially across the image data such that a region corresponding to the detected subject is processed according to parameters optimized for that category of subject, while remaining regions are processed according to default or alternative parameters. In this manner, the apparatus may, for instance, apply reduced noise reduction and increased sharpening to a region identified as containing a human face, thereby preserving perceptually significant detail.

### Advantages

The described configuration enables the imaging apparatus to produce image data having improved perceptual quality by adapting the image processing to the content of the captured scene, while efficiently utilizing processing resources by concentrating adaptive processing on regions of interest identified by the recognition support information.

---

# Image Sensor with Distributed Recognition Support

## Abstract

An image sensor apparatus and method are disclosed for reducing computational load on downstream image recognition processing. The image sensor includes an imaging surface configured to capture incident light and generate image data, wherein the imaging surface is logically partitioned into a plurality of discrete areas. A processing unit integrated with or coupled to the image sensor is configured to analyze each of the plurality of areas independently and generate support information corresponding to each respective area.

The support information may include preliminary classification data, feature indicators, region-of-interest designations, likelihood values, or attribute metadata characterizing image content within each area. By generating such support information at the sensor level, the apparatus offloads a portion of the recognition workload that would otherwise be performed entirely by an external recognition processor or host system.

In operation, the image sensor transmits the captured image data together with the generated support information to a subsequent recognition stage. The recognition stage utilizes the support information to selectively allocate processing resources, prioritize designated areas, bypass areas lacking relevant content, or otherwise constrain the scope of recognition operations. As a result, the volume of data requiring full recognition analysis is reduced, thereby decreasing processing time, power consumption, and bandwidth requirements of the overall system.

In certain embodiments, the division of the imaging surface into areas is dynamically adjustable based on prior recognition results, scene characteristics, or external control signals, enabling adaptive distribution of recognition-related tasks between the image sensor and downstream processing components.
